title: Egress path latency autopsy - short-run trace notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick runbook-style autopsy of a set of end-to-end traces showing elevated egress latency on the hosted API (recent spike during 2025-02-12 09:00-11:00 PT). These notes capture raw trace observations, hypotheses, quick experiments, and short-term mitigations. Focus is on stage-level splits (ingest / tokenize / kv-cache / model-forward / pack/postprocess / network-egress) and p50/p95/p99 behavior by sequence-length buckets.

Summary of user-facing symptom:
- Customers reported intermittent p95 regressions from ~180ms to ~380ms for small chat completions (avg seqlen ~64 tokens). p50 remained ~120ms. p99 increased up to ~720ms during the incident window.

Data sources examined:
- e2e traces pulled from trace-aggregator (TRACE-7894) filter: model_variant:rw-gpt-large, region:us-west-2, timeframe: 2025-02-12T08:40..2025-02-12T11:10
- Per-stage timing from runtime-span schema (ingest, tokenize, kv_lookup, forward, postprocess, network_send)
- GPU-side perf counters (kernel durations, memcpyH2D, memcpyD2H) sampled from metrics exporter
- Pod logs for cold-start events and scheduling anomalies

Trace-level aggregated numbers (sample from 2,134 traces):
- All traces: p50 119ms, p95 342ms, p99 681ms
- Short seqlen (<=64): p50 110ms, p95 378ms, p99 690ms
- Medium seqlen (65-256): p50 190ms, p95 410ms, p99 820ms
- Long seqlen (>256): p50 410ms, p95 840ms, p99 1600ms

Per-stage median contribution (global):
- ingest: 4ms (median) / 12ms (p95)
- tokenize: 9ms / 18ms
- kv_lookup: 6ms / 24ms
- forward (model kernels + scheduling): 72ms / 250ms
- postprocess/pack: 6ms / 40ms
- network_send (egress to client + flush): 18ms / 60ms
Notes: model forward dominates p95/p99 tail. But forward alone does not fully account for the observed p99; postprocess and network_send tails contribute in many traces.

Important trace pattern observed (frequent):
- Cold-GPU-start traces: significantly higher memcpyH2D and kernel queue wait time visible. Example trace sample (short seqlen): ingest:3 / tokenize:10 / kv:7 / memcpyH2D:85ms / forward-kernels:60ms / queue-wait:120ms / postprocess:6 / network:12 => total ~303ms. These traces cluster at pod warmup times (autoscaler launching new container) and align with CPU scheduling jitter.

Hypotheses and evidence:
1) Cold start memcpy + queue wait explains a large fraction of p95 spikes for short requests. Evidence: high correlation (r=0.76) between memcpyH2D duration and trace latency for traces where pod_age < 60s. GPU occupancy low for these traces.
2) KV-cache misses cause synchronous CPU work that blocks batching windows, inflating forward latency for medium length requests. Evidence: traces with kv_miss=true show 2x higher tokenize+kv combined time and then longer wait before kernel launch.
3) Network egress/multiplexing: gRPC flush delays at the edge cause p99 skew in some cross-region flows. Evidence: network_send p99 spikes correspond to gRPC dial/keepalive logs showing delayed ACKs during 09:30-09:50 window.

Detailed micro-observations:
- Kernel launch stalls: traces show intervals labelled "queue_wait" representing time between enqueuing kernel and actual kernel start. When queue_wait > 80ms, model forward is effectively 2-3x slower in p95 bucket.
- memcpyH2D outliers: a subset of traces (approx 7%) have memcpyH2D > 80ms. These are always associated with recent pod boot and coincide with HBM cache reinitialization in the driver.
- Batching confounding: continuous-batching turned on at this variant with aggressive max_batch_latency=30ms. For kv_cache-miss traces the batching window expired when CPU-side kv lookup took 40-120ms, causing single-request kernels (no batching) with relatively high per-request overhead.

Quick experiments run (2025-02-12 13:00–14:00):
- Disabled continuous batching for a subset of pods (canary): p95 decreased from 378ms -> 320ms for short seqlen group on canary but throughput dropped ~4%. Indication: aggressive batching can worsen tail when CPU-side blocking occurs.
- Pre-warm step: added a H2D dummy memcpy after pod start to force driver path warmup; reduced memcpyH2D outliers from 7% to 1.9% across test traces.
- KV async attempt: started an async KV lookup prototype (not yet in prod). On short experiment, kv-miss traces reduced forward delay by ~22% but required thread pool tuning.

Actionable short-term mitigations (next 72 hours):
- Deploy driver warmup patch: on container start trigger a small H2D copy and dummy kernel to prime the driver and stabilize memcpyH2D times. Owner: Marcus Huang. ETA: 48h.
- Reduce max_batch_latency from 30ms -> 15ms for rw-gpt-large variant in region us-west-2 to reduce tail waiting for CPU-side kv work. Owner: Lina Gomez. ETA: 24h to roll canary, monitor p95 impact.
- Add a pod_age tag and exclude pod_age < 60s traces from SLAs for 48h while we roll warmup. Owner: SRE (ticket JIRA-RT-4423). ETA: 6h.

Longer-term work (planning):
- Migrate KV lookup path to asynchronous worker threads + prefetch to avoid blocking batching window. Requires API and memory-safety audit. Owner: eng-applied-ml. Est. 4 sprint.
- Investigate queue-wait root cause: is it driver VM scheduling, host CPU starvation, or CUDA stream contention? Plan: collect low-level GPU scheduler logs and host perf during tail events. Owner: infra-team. Est. 2 sprints.
- Revisit batching strategy: add adaptive batching that is KV-awareness aware (short-circuit when cpu-side blocking is detected). Integrate into Optimize heuristics. Owner: product-optimize. Est. 3 sprints.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do some pod restarts still show memcpyH2D outliers after warmup patch (investigate kernel residency and driver version diffs).
- Is any network egress tail caused by customer-side slow clients (client windowing) vs. our gRPC implementation? Need packet captures for a couple of p99 traces.
- Correlation with on-host CPU steal or noisy neighbors during 09:30 window — need host-level metrics aligned with trace timestamps.

Quick trace examples (anonymized timestamps):
- trace A (pod_age 18s): ingest:3 tokenize:12 kv:8 memcpyH2D:98 queue_wait:132 forward_kernels:64 post:4 network:10 total:331ms (p95 sample)
- trace B (pod_age 7d): ingest:2 tokenize:9 kv:2 memcpyH2D:9 queue_wait:6 forward_kernels:68 post:5 network:11 total:102ms (p50 sample)

Monitoring / alerting changes recommended:
- New metric: perc_pod_warmup_memcpy_over_80ms count by model_variant — alert if > 0.5% over 15m.
- Add trace sampling rule to capture full GPU profiler snapshots for traces where queue_wait > 50ms.

Next steps (owners and dates):
- Marcus: implement warmup patch and land PR -> link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3321. Target merge: 2025-02-18.
- Lina: roll reduced batch latency on canary (us-west-2) and report p50/p95 changes. Target: 2025-02-16.
- Priya: run KV async experiment with wider threadpool (staging) and produce perf diff. Target: 2025-02-28.
- Infra: collect NVidia driver and host perf logs for 09:20-09:50 window and correlate. Target: 2025-02-21.

Appendix: recommended quick command snippets
- Query sample traces by pod_age and memcpyH2D:
  SELECT trace_id, pod_age_s, stage_timings, gpu_events FROM traces WHERE model_variant='rw-gpt-large' AND timestamp >= '2025-02-12T08:40' AND memcpyH2D > 50 ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 200;

- Capture full GPU profiler for a sampled trace id (internal tool):
  profiler-capture --trace-id <TRACE_ID> --duration 30s --output /tmp/prof.tar

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working autopsy (not final incident report). I prioritized quick experiments and short-term mitigations likely to move the needle fast. Please add contradictory evidence or other reproduction notes inline.

-- Ethan
